title: Gurmukhi Orthography & Mukta/Laga Matra
subtitle: Understanding inherent vowels and diacritic markers
keyPoint: Every bare Gurmukhi consonant contains an inherent short vowel called 'Mukta' unless modified or replaced by a dependent vowel sign (Laga Matra).

mistakes.note: Short 'i' requires the Sihari marker (ਿ) placed to the left of the consonant.
Word-final long 'ee' sounds require Bihari (ੀ), not Sihari.
Do not add Kanna (ਾ) if the word ends with the inherent mukta sound.

quiz.question: Which word contains only the inherent Mukta vowel?
quiz.explanation: 'ਘਰ' consists solely of two consonants carrying the inherent short Mukta vowel.

quiz.question: Complete the word for 'book': '___ਤਾਬ'
quiz.explanation: The word 'ਕਿਤਾਬ' takes Sihari (ਿ) before the consonant 'ਕ' for the short /ɪ/ sound.

quiz.question: Identify the vowel sign used at the end of 'ਪਾਣੀ':
quiz.explanation: The stroke on the right side of 'ਣ' is Bihari (ੀ), denoting a long /iː/ vowel.

quiz.question: Which word correctly spells 'black' using Kanna?
quiz.explanation: 'ਕਾਲਾ' correctly uses Kanna on both syllables for the long /aː/ sounds.

tip: Remember that Sihari is visually written to the left of a consonant, but phonetically pronounced after it!

title: Direct vs Oblique Noun Inflection
subtitle: Inflecting nouns before postpositions
keyPoint: Marked masculine singular nouns ending in Kanna (-ਾ) change to Laan (-ੇ) before any postposition, while plurals typically add '-ਆਂ'.

mistakes.note: Marked masculine singular nouns like 'ਮੁੰਡਾ' must shift to 'ਮੁੰਡੇ' before postpositions like 'ਨੇ'.

mistakes.wrong: ਮੁੰਡੇ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਣੀ ਦਿਓ। (to the boys)
mistakes.note: For masculine plural oblique before postpositions, use '-ਆਂ' ('ਮੁੰਡਿਆਂ'), not the direct plural ending.
Singular 'ਕਮਰਾ' takes the oblique ending '-ੇ' when followed by 'ਵਿੱਚ'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: '___ ਨੇ ਦੁੱਧ ਪੀਤਾ।' (The boy drank milk)
quiz.explanation: The singular marked masculine noun 'ਮੁੰਡਾ' shifts to oblique 'ਮੁੰਡੇ' before the postposition 'ਨੇ'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct oblique plural form: 'Give books to the girls' -> '___ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਤਾਬਾਂ ਦਿਓ।'
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in '-ੀ' take '-ੀਆਂ' in both direct plural and oblique plural.

quiz.question: What is the oblique singular form of 'ਕਮਰਾ' (room)?
quiz.explanation: Marked masculine nouns replace final '-ਾ' with '-ੇ' in the oblique singular.

quiz.question: Choose the correct oblique plural for 'ਘਰ' (house): 'ਉਹ ___ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ।' (in the houses)
quiz.explanation: Unmarked masculine nouns add '-ਾਂ' to form the oblique plural.

tip: Any time a noun is directly followed by a particle (ਨੂੰ, ਨੇ, ਵਿੱਚ, ਤੋਂ, ਦਾ), check if it needs an oblique ending!

title: Core Postpositions & The Genitive 'Daa'
subtitle: Expressing possession and relational location
keyPoint: The genitive postposition agrees in gender and number with the possessed noun that follows it: ਦਾ, ਦੇ, ਦੀ, or ਦੀਆਂ.

examples.en: ਰਾਜ ਦਾ ਘਰ ਬਹੁਤ ਵੱਡਾ ਹੈ।
ਉਸ ਦੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਮੇਜ਼ 'ਤੇ ਪਈ ਹੈ।

mistakes.note: 'ਕਿਤਾਬ' is feminine singular, so the genitive postposition must be 'ਦੀ', not 'ਦਾ'.
'ਕੱਪੜੇ' is masculine plural, so it requires 'ਦੇ' instead of 'ਦਾ'.
Do not chain 'ਦਾ' redundantly after spatial postpositions like 'ਉੱਤੇ'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'ਇਹ ਮੇਰੇ ਵੀਰ ___ ਕਾਰ ਹੈ।' (This is my brother's car - feminine)
quiz.explanation: Since 'ਕਾਰ' is feminine singular, the genitive postposition must agree with it as 'ਦੀ'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct genitive marker: 'ਕੁੜੀ ___ ਖਿਡੌਣੇ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹਨ?' (Where are the girl's toys? - masc. plural)
quiz.explanation: Toys ('ਖਿਡੌਣੇ') is masculine plural, demanding the masculine plural form 'ਦੇ'.

quiz.question: Which postposition corresponds to 'from' in 'from the shop'?
quiz.explanation: 'ਤੋਂ' means 'from' or 'since' in Punjabi.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ___ ਪੁੱਛੋ।' (Ask the teacher - recipient)
quiz.explanation: 'ਨੂੰ' marks the direct/indirect object or recipient of an action.

tip: Always look ahead to the possessed object (not the possessor) to choose between ਦਾ, ਦੇ, ਦੀ, or ਦੀਆਂ.

title: Personal Pronouns & Irregular Oblique Stems
subtitle: Using subject pronouns and oblique stems
keyPoint: Personal pronouns take distinct oblique stems before postpositions (e.g., ਮੈਂ becomes ਮੈ- / ਮੇਰੇ, ਤੂੰ becomes ਤੈ- / ਤੇਰੇ, ਉਹ becomes ਉਸ / ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ).

mistakes.note: 'ਮੈਂ + ਨੂੰ' fuses into the oblique contraction 'ਮੈਨੂੰ'.
Singular 'ਉਹ' becomes oblique 'ਉਸ' before postpositions like 'ਨੇ'.
Use 'ਤੈਨੂੰ' instead of placing the bare direct pronoun 'ਤੂੰ' with 'ਨੂੰ'.

quiz.question: What is the correct form for 'to me': '___ ਦੱਸੋ।' (Tell me)?
quiz.explanation: 'ਮੈਂ' merges with postposition 'ਨੂੰ' to form 'ਮੈਨੂੰ'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank with the singular oblique pronoun: '___ ਨੇ ਕੰਮ ਮੁਕਾਇਆ।' (He/She finished work)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular pronoun 'ਉਹ' takes the oblique stem 'ਉਸ' before 'ਨੇ'.

quiz.question: Which form represents 'to us'?
quiz.explanation: 'ਅਸੀਂ + ਨੂੰ' contracts irregularly into 'ਸਾਨੂੰ'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct polite/plural possessive for 'Your': 'ਇਹ ___ ਘਰ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: 'ਤੁਹਾਡਾ' is the formal/plural 2nd-person possessive adjective agreeing with masculine 'ਘਰ'.

tip: Think of ਮੈਨੂੰ (to me), ਤੈਨੂੰ (to you), and ਸਾਨੂੰ (to us) as single indivisible words rather than separate pronouns plus postpositions.

title: The Copula 'Hona' & Negation with 'Nahi'
subtitle: Expressing 'to be' and negating assertions
keyPoint: The auxiliary verb 'ਹੋਣਾ' conjugates to match subject person and number, and negation particle 'ਨਹੀਂ' is typically placed immediately before the copula.

mistakes.note: First person 'ਮੈਂ' must take 'ਹਾਂ', never third-person 'ਹੈ'.
In standard SOV sentences, 'ਨਹੀਂ' precedes the copula at the end rather than standing at the very beginning.
Third person plural 'ਉਹ' pairs with 'ਹਨ', while 'ਹੋ' is reserved for 'ਤੁਸੀਂ'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'ਮੈਂ ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ___।' (I am a teacher)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular pronoun 'ਮੈਂ' conjugates with 'ਹਾਂ'.

quiz.question: Select the correct copula for plural/respectful: 'ਉਹ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ___।' (They are in the market)
quiz.explanation: 3rd person plural/honorific subjects require 'ਹਨ'.

quiz.question: Negate the sentence correctly: 'ਉਹ ਘਰ ਹੈ।' -> 'He is not home.'
quiz.explanation: Standard negation places 'ਨਹੀਂ' right before the final copula: 'ਉਹ ਘਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।'

quiz.question: Complete the question: 'ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕੌਣ ___?' (Who are you?)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person plural/formal pronoun 'ਤੁਸੀਂ' pairs with 'ਹੋ'.

tip: In conversational Punjabi, the present copula (ਹੈ, ਹਨ) is often dropped after ਨਹੀਂ (e.g., 'ਮੈਨੂੰ ਪਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ' instead of 'ਮੈਨੂੰ ਪਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ').

title: Habitual Aspect Markers (-ਦਾ, -ਦੀ, -ਦੇ)
subtitle: Talking about daily habits and recurring routines
keyPoint: Add gender and number agreement suffixes (-ਦਾ, -ਦੀ, -ਦੇ, -ਦੀਆਂ) directly to the verb stem followed by the auxiliary 'ਹੋਣਾ' to express habitual actions.

useCases.label: Daily Routines
useCases.example: ਮੈਂ ਰੋਜ਼ ਸਵੇਰੇ ਚਾਹ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ।

examples.en: ਮੈਂ ਹਰ ਰੋਜ਼ ਸੈਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ।

mistakes.note: The verb participle must agree with the feminine singular subject by using -ਦੀ, not -ਦਾ.
Do not omit the present auxiliary 'ਹਾਂ' in standard habitual affirmative statements.
Feminine plural subjects require the distinctive plural feminine ending -ਦੀਆਂ.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct feminine singular form: 'ਰਾਧਾ ਗੀਤ ___ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: Radha is feminine singular, so the verb takes the suffix -ਦੀ.

quiz.question: Select the correct masculine plural verb: 'ਮੁੰਡੇ ਸਕੂਲ ___ ਹਨ।'
quiz.explanation: Boys (ਮੁੰਡੇ) is masculine plural, requiring the suffix -ਦੇ.

quiz.question: Choose the feminine plural form: 'ਕੁੜੀਆਂ ਹਾਕੀ ___ ਹਨ।'
quiz.explanation: Girls (ਕੁੜੀਆਂ) is feminine plural, which requires -ਦੀਆਂ.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence for a male speaker: 'ਮੈਂ ਪਾਣੀ ___ ਹਾਂ।'
quiz.explanation: A masculine singular speaker uses -ਦਾ followed by ਹਾਂ.

tip: Remember that unlike Hindi, Punjabi retains a distinct feminine plural participle ending (-ਦੀਆਂ) instead of collapsing plural agreement into the auxiliary.

title: Simple Past & Ergative 'ਨੇ' Usage
subtitle: Mastering transitive past constructions and ergative alignment
keyPoint: In the simple past tense, transitive verbs require the ergative postposition 'ਨੇ' after the agent, causing the verb to agree with the object instead of the subject.

useCases.label: Completed Transitive Action
useCases.example: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਇੱਕ ਚੰਗੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਪੜ੍ਹੀ।

mistakes.note: The noun preceding 'ਨੇ' must inflect into the oblique case ('ਮੁੰਡੇ' instead of 'ਮੁੰਡਾ').
Because the verb is transitive, it agrees with the feminine object 'ਕਿਤਾਬ' (ਪੜ੍ਹੀ), not the subject.
'ਜਾਣਾ' (to go) is intransitive in Punjabi and never takes the ergative marker 'ਨੇ'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct past verb for: 'ਕੁੜੀ ਨੇ ਰੋਟੀ ___।'
quiz.explanation: The feminine object 'ਰੋਟੀ' requires the feminine singular past form 'ਖਾਧੀ'.

quiz.question: Select the correct form of the agent before 'ਨੇ': '___ ਨੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਤਾ।'
quiz.explanation: Before the postposition 'ਨੇ', the singular noun 'ਮੁੰਡਾ' changes to the oblique form 'ਮੁੰਡੇ'.

quiz.question: Identify the sentence with an intransitive verb (no 'ਨੇ'):
quiz.explanation: 'ਆਉਣਾ' (to come) is intransitive, so the subject remains unmarked without 'ਨੇ'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the plural feminine past verb: 'ਮਾਂ ਨੇ ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ ___।'
quiz.explanation: 'ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ' is feminine plural, so the agreeing transitive verb must be 'ਸੁਣਾਈਆਂ'.

tip: Always check transitivity first: if the action cannot take a direct object (like ਸੌਣਾ, ਜਾਣਾ, ਆਉਣਾ), never use 'ਨੇ'!

title: Continuous Aspect with 'ਰਿਹਾ'
subtitle: Describing actions in progress across present and past
keyPoint: Form the continuous aspect by combining the bare verb root with the auxiliary participle 'ਰਿਹਾ/ਰਹੀ/ਰਹੇ/ਰਹੀਆਂ' and the appropriate tense marker.

useCases.label: Ongoing Temporary States
useCases.example: ਅਸੀਂ ਅੱਜ-ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸਿੱਖ ਰਹੇ ਹਾਂ।

mistakes.note: Use the bare verb root (ਪੜ੍ਹ), not the habitual participle (ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ), before 'ਰਿਹਾ'.
'ਰਿਹਾ' must change to 'ਰਹੀ' to agree with a feminine singular subject.
When the subject is feminine plural, 'ਰਹੀ' must inflect to 'ਰਹੀਆਂ'.

quiz.question: Complete the feminine singular sentence: 'ਮਾਤਾ ਜੀ ਖਾਣਾ ਬਣਾ ___ ਹਨ।'
quiz.explanation: Mother (ਮਾਤਾ ਜੀ) is feminine, taking the agreement marker 'ਰਹੀ' (with honorific plural auxiliary ਹਨ).

quiz.question: Select the correct form for multiple men: 'ਮੁੰਡੇ ਫੁੱਟਬਾਲ ਖੇਡ ___ ਸਨ।'
quiz.explanation: Masculine plural subjects require 'ਰਹੇ'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for a group of girls: 'ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥਣਾਂ ਪੜ੍ਹ ___ ਹਨ।'
quiz.explanation: Female students (ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥਣਾਂ) is feminine plural, so 'ਰਹੀਆਂ' is mandatory.

quiz.question: Complete the question for a male listener: 'ਤੂੰ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਜਾ ___ ਹੈਂ?'
quiz.explanation: Addressing a single male informal subject (ਤੂੰ) requires 'ਰਿਹਾ'.

tip: Keep the main verb in its bare root form (ਜਾ, ਖਾ, ਪੀ, ਕਰ) without adding any inflections before 'ਰਿਹਾ'.

title: Synthetic Future Tense Conjugation
subtitle: Forming future statements without auxiliary verbs
keyPoint: Punjabi forms its future tense synthetically by attaching suffix endings (-ਏਗਾ, -ਏਗੀ, -ਾਂਗਾ, -ਾਂਗੇ) directly to the verb stem without auxiliary verbs.

mistakes.note: Punjabi future is synthetic; never add the present auxiliary 'ਹਾਂ' to future inflected verbs.
Third person feminine singular requires the feminine future marker -ੇਗੀ.
First person plural ('ਅਸੀਂ') requires the ending -ਾਂਗੇ.

quiz.question: Complete for a female speaker: 'ਮੈਂ ਚਿੱਠੀ ___।'
quiz.explanation: A female first-person speaker ('ਮੈਂ') uses the ending -ਾਂਗੀ (ਲਿਖਾਂਗੀ).

quiz.question: Select the verb for 3rd person masculine singular: 'ਸੋਹਣ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਕੰਮ ___।'
quiz.explanation: Third person masculine singular takes -ੇਗਾ (ਕਰੇਗਾ).

quiz.question: Choose the plural form: 'ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ___।'
quiz.explanation: 'ਅਸੀਂ' (we) requires the plural future suffix -ਾਂਗੇ (ਜਾਵਾਂਗੇ).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'ਕੁੜੀਆਂ ਮੈਦਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ___।'
quiz.explanation: Feminine plural third-person subjects take -ਣਗੀਆਂ / -ਨਗੀਆਂ (ਦੌੜਨਗੀਆਂ).

tip: Notice how Punjabi merges the tense, gender, and person into a single synthetic word, completely dropping auxiliaries like 'ਹੈ' or 'ਸੀ'.

title: Locative & Directional Postpositions (ਵੱਲੋਂ, ਕੰਨ, ਕੋਲੇ)
subtitle: Expressing directions, sources, and spatial proximity
keyPoint: Directional and locative postpositions like 'ਵੱਲ' (towards), 'ਵੱਲੋਂ' (from/by), and 'ਕੋਲ' (near/with) follow nouns in the oblique case or the genitive linker 'ਦੇ'.

examples.en: ਉਹ ਸਕੂਲ ਦੇ ਵੱਲ ਤੁਰ ਪਿਆ।
ਨਦੀ ਦੇ ਕੰਨੇ ਵੱਡੇ ਰੁੱਖ ਹਨ।

mistakes.note: Personal pronouns take genitive/oblique base forms (ਮੇਰੇ, ਤੇਰੇ, ਸਾਡੇ) before 'ਕੋਲ'.
Spatial postpositions require the oblique genitive linker 'ਦੇ', never the direct masculine 'ਦਾ'.
Use 'ਵੱਲ' for direction 'towards'; 'ਵੱਲੋਂ' means 'from' or 'via'.

quiz.question: Select the correct phrase for 'towards home': 'ਉਹ ਘਰ ___ ਗਿਆ।'
quiz.explanation: 'ਵੱਲ' denotes direction towards a destination.

quiz.question: Choose the correct possessive construct for 'with me / I have': '___ ਕੋਲ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: The postposition 'ਕੋਲ' requires the oblique pronoun form 'ਮੇਰੇ'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence meaning 'from our side': 'ਇਹ ਮਦਦ ਸਾਡੇ ___ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: 'ਵੱਲੋਂ' translates to 'from' or 'on behalf of'.

quiz.question: Select the correct phrase meaning 'near the shop': 'ਦੁਕਾਨ ___ ਖੜ੍ਹੋ।'
quiz.explanation: Compound postpositions use the oblique connector 'ਦੇ' (ਦੇ ਕੋਲ).

tip: Remember that '-ਓਂ' at the end of postpositions like 'ਵੱਲੋਂ' acts like the ablative suffix 'from', contrasting with 'ਵੱਲ' which means 'towards'.

title: Basic Subjunctive Mood
subtitle: Forming wishes, doubts, suggestions, and polite queries
keyPoint: The subjunctive is formed by adding personal inflection endings directly to the verb root without any auxiliary verbs.

cells: Shall I go? / May I go
Let us see / Should we see
May you speak / That they speak

useCases.label: Wishes and Hopes
useCases.example: ਰੱਬ ਕਰੇ ਉਹ ਇਮਤਿਹਾਨ ਪਾਸ ਕਰੇ।

examples.en: ਹੋ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੱਜ ਮੀਂਹ ਪਵੇ।
ਕੀ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਦਦ ਕਰੋਗੇ ਜਾਂ ਮੈਂ ਇਕੱਲਾ ਕਰਾਂ?
ਚੰਗਾ ਹੋਵੇਗਾ ਜੇ ਉਹ ਸਮੇਂ ਸਿਰ ਆਉਣ।

mistakes.wrong: ਕੀ ਮੈਂ ਹੁਣ ਅੰਦਰ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ?
mistakes.note: Using the present habitual tense sounds like stating a fact instead of politely asking for permission.
Do not use the infinitive structure when suggesting a collective action; use the subjunctive first-person plural ending -ਈਏ.
After uncertainty words like ਸ਼ਾਇਦ (maybe/perhaps), use the subjunctive rather than the definite future tense.

quiz.question: Politely ask: 'Shall I bring water?' -> ਕੀ ਮੈਂ ਪਾਣੀ ___?
quiz.explanation: For the pronoun ਮੈਂ in a polite subjunctive query, use the root + -ਆਂ ending (ਲਿਆਵਾਂ).

quiz.question: Suggest: 'Let us eat food.' -> ਆਓ ਰੋਟੀ ___।
quiz.explanation: The cohortative/collective suggestion for 'we' takes the subjunctive ending -ਈਏ (ਖਾਈਏ).

quiz.question: Express uncertainty: 'Maybe he will speak today.' -> ਸ਼ਾਇਦ ਉਹ ਅੱਜ ___।
quiz.explanation: With ਸ਼ਾਇਦ, Punjabi prefers the third-person singular subjunctive verb ending in -ਏ (ਬੋਲੇ).

quiz.question: Ask for advice: 'What should we do now?' -> ਹੁਣ ਅਸੀਂ ਕੀ ___?
quiz.explanation: The first-person plural pronoun ਅਸੀਂ requires the subjunctive form ਕਰੀਏ.

tip: To make any suggestion sound polite and natural in Punjabi, simply strip the future -ਗਾ/-ਗੇ endings and use the bare subjunctive suffix.

title: Imperative Tiers & Respect Levels
subtitle: Mastering intimate, familiar, and highly respectful commands
keyPoint: Punjabi imperatives strictly mirror social hierarchy using three distinct forms: bare root for intimate 'ਤੂੰ', -ਓ for familiar 'ਤੁਸੀਂ', and -ਇਓ / -ਓ ਜੀ for deferential requests.

cells: Close peers, younger relatives, or children
Standard polite command for equals and elders
Gentle request or instruction for future action

examples.en: ਤੂੰ ਮੇਰੀ ਗੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣ।
ਜਦੋਂ ਵੇਹਲੇ ਹੋਵੋ ਤਾਂ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਿਓ।

mistakes.note: Pairing the plural/respectful pronoun ਤੁਸੀਂ with the bare root command ਆ sounds disrespectful.
Bare root imperatives should never be addressed to parents or elders.
Use ਨਾ (or ਨਹੀਂ) rather than Hindi 'ਮਤ' for negative commands in Punjabi.

quiz.question: Politely ask your teacher to sit: 'Teacher, please ___ here.' -> ਮਾਸਟਰ ਜੀ, ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ ਏਥੇ ___।
quiz.explanation: Addressing an elder or teacher requires the polite -ਓ ending (ਬੈਠੋ).

quiz.question: Tell your younger brother casually: 'Look there!' -> ਓਧਰ ___!
quiz.explanation: For intimate/younger addressees (ਤੂੰ level), the bare verb stem ਦੇਖ is used.

quiz.question: Instruct gently for later: 'Call me tomorrow.' -> ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਫ਼ੋਨ ___।
quiz.explanation: The -ਇਓ suffix (ਕਰਿਓ) conveys a gentle or delayed/future imperative instruction.

quiz.question: What is the respectful negative command: 'Please do not speak loudly.' -> ਉੱਚੀ ___?
quiz.explanation: The polite negative command combines the standard particle ਨਾ with the polite plural imperative ਬੋਲੋ.

tip: When in doubt, always use the -ਓ ending. It is courteous enough for strangers and natural enough not to sound stiff.

title: Conjunctive Participle (-ਕੇ)
subtitle: Connecting chronological actions seamlessly with 'having done'
keyPoint: Attach -ਕੇ (or -ਕਰਕੇ) directly to a verb stem to indicate an action completed immediately prior to the main clause verb.

cells: Read the book and went to sleep
Having finished work, we will leave
Take a bath and get ready

useCases.label: Sequential Actions
useCases.example: ਉਹ ਚਾਹ ਪੀ ਕੇ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਗਿਆ।

useCases.label: Reason / Cause
useCases.example: ਬਿਮਾਰ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਉਹ ਸਕੂਲ ਨਾ ਆਇਆ।

examples.en: ਉਹ ਹੱਥ ਧੋ ਕੇ ਖਾਣਾ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਮੈਂ ਘਰ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਕੇ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਸੁਨੇਹਾ ਭੇਜਾਂਗਾ।
ਬੱਚੇ ਸਕੂਲੋਂ ਆ ਕੇ ਖੇਡਣ ਲੱਗੇ।
ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੀ ਗੱਲ ਸੁਣ ਕੇ ਹੈਰਾਨ ਰਹਿ ਗਏ।

mistakes.wrong: ਉਹ ਖਾਣਾ ਖਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਗਿਆ।
mistakes.right: ਉਹ ਖਾਣਾ ਖਾ ਕੇ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਗਿਆ।
mistakes.note: Chaining full verbs with 'ਅਤੇ' sounds unnatural when the same subject carries out sequential actions; use -ਕੇ instead.
Attach -ਕੇ to the bare verb root (ਪੜ੍ਹ), not to the infinitive (ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ).
Never conjugate the first verb into past tense before -ਕੇ.

quiz.question: Combine into one clause: 'Having washed hands, eat.' -> ਹੱਥ ___ ਰੋਟੀ ਖਾਓ।
quiz.explanation: The conjunctive participle attaches ਕੇ directly to the root ਧੋ to give ਧੋ ਕੇ.

quiz.question: Express sequence: 'I will call after reaching home.' -> ਮੈਂ ਘਰ ___ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਕਰਾਂਗਾ।
quiz.explanation: ਪਹੁੰਚ ਕੇ ('having reached') links the prior action to the main future verb.

quiz.question: Complete the instruction: 'Think carefully before speaking.' -> ਸੋਚ ___ ਬੋਲੋ।
quiz.explanation: The common Punjabi paired idiom is ਸੋਚ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ('having thought and understood').

quiz.question: Choose the correct prior action: 'He took the medicine and slept.' -> ਉਹ ਦਵਾਈ ___ ਸੌਂ ਗਿਆ।
quiz.explanation: The root of ਲੈਣਾ is ਲੈ, resulting in ਲੈ ਕੇ ('having taken').

tip: If the base verb itself is ਕਰਨਾ (to do), use ਕਰਕੇ (having done), which also doubles as the everyday word for 'because of'.

title: Compound Verbs & Vector Auxiliaries
subtitle: Adding direction, finality, and attitude using vector verbs
keyPoint: In a compound verb, the main verb appears as a bare stem carrying meaning, while the auxiliary vector verb takes all grammatical inflections to specify nuance.

cells: He gave away the money completely
He ripped up the letter recklessly

useCases.label: Inward Reflexive Action
useCases.example: ਮੈਂ ਇਹ ਪਾਠ ਯਾਦ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ।

useCases.label: Outward Directed Action
useCases.example: ਮੈਂ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਦੱਸ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

examples.en: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਆਪਣਾ ਕੰਮ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰ ਲਵੋ।

mistakes.note: Giving outward to someone else requires the vector ਦੇਣਾ, not the inward-oriented ਲੈਣਾ.
The primary verb must stay in its bare stem form (ਚਲ), while only the vector inflects (ਗਿਆ).
Compound vectors are rarely used in standard negative sentences; use the simple past instead.

quiz.question: Complete the inward action: 'I bought and kept the book for myself.' -> ਮੈਂ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਖ਼ਰੀਦ ___।
quiz.explanation: Actions carried out for one's own advantage take the vector verb ਲੈਣਾ (feminine past: ਲਈ).

quiz.question: Complete the outward action: 'I told him the secret.' -> ਮੈਂ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਭੇਤ ਦੱਸ ___।
quiz.explanation: An action directed towards someone else takes the vector ਦੇਣਾ (masculine past: ਦਿੱਤਾ).

quiz.question: Indicate irreversible completion: 'The glass broke.' -> ਗਲਾਸ ਟੁੱਟ ___।
quiz.explanation: Intransitive changes of state and irreversible events take the vector verb ਜਾਣਾ (past: ਗਿਆ).

quiz.question: Identify the vector verb in this sentence: 'ਉਸਨੇ ਕੰਮ ਮੁਕਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ।' -> Which word is the vector?
quiz.explanation: ਮੁਕਾ is the primary verb stem ('to finish'), while ਦਿੱਤਾ is the inflected vector auxiliary imparting completion.

tip: Think of ਲੈਣਾ as 'pulling the benefit in towards you' and ਦੇਣਾ as 'pushing the action outward to someone else'.

title: First & Second Causative Verbs
subtitle: Deriving actions made to happen directly or through an intermediary
keyPoint: Punjabi systematically derives transitive verbs using -ਆਉਣਾ (-auna) for direct causation and -ਵਾਉਣਾ (-vauna) for indirect causation through an agent.

cells: Do -> Have done -> Get done by someone
Eat -> Feed -> Cause to be fed

useCases.label: Caregiving / Feeding
useCases.example: ਮਾਂ ਬੱਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਟੀ ਖੁਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

examples.en: ਮੈਂ ਮਿਸਤਰੀ ਕੋਲੋਂ ਕਾਰ ਠੀਕ ਕਰਵਾਈ।
ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਇਹ ਪਤਾ ਸਮਝਾਓ।
ਡਾਕਟਰ ਨੇ ਮਰੀਜ਼ ਨੂੰ ਦਵਾਈ ਪਿਲਾਈ।

mistakes.right: ਮੈਂ ਬੱਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਖਾਣਾ ਖੁਆਉਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ।
mistakes.note: Using ਖਾਣਾ means you are eating, whereas the first causative ਖੁਆਉਣਾ means you are feeding someone else.
The person performing the labor takes the postposition ਤੋਂ or ਕੋਲੋਂ, while the initiator is the subject.
ਹੱਸਣਾ is intransitive ('to laugh'); making someone else laugh requires the causative stem ਹਸਾਉਣਾ.

quiz.question: Say 'The teacher teaches Punjabi' -> ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ___ ਹੈ।
quiz.explanation: The direct causative of ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ ('to read') is ਪੜ੍ਹਾਉਣਾ ('to teach/cause to learn').

quiz.question: Say 'I got the house painted by a painter' -> ਮੈਂ ਰੰਗਸਾਜ਼ ਤੋਂ ਘਰ ਰੰਗ___।
quiz.explanation: Indirect causation involving a paid agent takes the second causative suffix -ਵਾਇਆ (ਰੰਗਵਾਇਆ).

quiz.question: Choose the correct causative for 'to show' derived from ਦੇਖਣਾ (to see):
quiz.explanation: The standard first causative of ਦੇਖਣਾ (to see) with vowel shortening is ਦਿਖਾਉਣਾ (to show).

quiz.question: What role does the postposition 'ਤੋਂ' play in: 'ਮੈਂ ਨੌਕਰ ਤੋਂ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਵਾਇਆ'?
quiz.explanation: In second causative sentences, the secondary agent who executes the physical task is marked by ਤੋਂ or ਕੋਲੋਂ.

tip: Long vowels in the root often shorten when forming causatives: ਖਾਣਾ becomes ਖੁਆਉਣਾ, and ਪੀਣਾ becomes ਪਿਆਉਣਾ/ਪਿਲਾਉਣਾ.

title: Modalities of Obligation ('Paina' vs 'Chahida')
subtitle: Distinguishing external compulsion from ethical advice using dative subjects
keyPoint: Both constructions require an oblique subject marked by ਨੂੰ, where ਪੈਣਾ denotes inescapable external compulsion and ਚਾਹੀਦਾ denotes moral advisability or desire.

useCases.label: External Duty
useCases.example: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਹਰ ਰੋਜ਼ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਜਾਣਾ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

useCases.label: Unavoidable Past Action
useCases.example: ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮੀਂਹ ਕਰਕੇ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਘਰ ਬੈਠਣਾ ਪਿਆ।

examples.en: ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਬਜ਼ੁਰਗਾਂ ਦਾ ਆਦਰ ਕਰਨਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੀ ਰਾਤ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਨਾ ਪਿਆ।
ਸਾਨੂੰ ਸਾਫ਼ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਣਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਬੱਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਕੂਲ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ ਸਮੇਂ ਸਿਰ ਕਰਨਾ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

mistakes.note: Obligation modals require the subject to take the dative postposition ਨੂੰ (ਮੈਨੂੰ, not ਮੈਂ).
When the verb has a direct object, both the infinitive stem and ਚਾਹੀਦਾ must agree in gender and number with that object.
Do not confuse the ergative marker ਨੇ with the dative marker ਨੂੰ needed for modals of compulsion.

quiz.question: Because of bad weather, we had to stay home: 'ਸਾਨੂੰ ਘਰ ਰਹਿਣਾ ___।'
quiz.explanation: ਪਿਆ marks unavoidable external past compulsion.

quiz.question: You should speak politely to others: 'ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ___।'
quiz.explanation: ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ marks moral recommendation rather than physical force.

quiz.question: I have to leave right now (obligation imposed by schedule): 'ਮੈਨੂੰ ਹੁਣੇ ___।'
quiz.explanation: ਜਾਣਾ ਪੈਣਾ ਹੈ (or ਜਾਣਾ ਪਵੇਗਾ) conveys scheduled external necessity.

quiz.question: We ought to read these newspapers: 'ਸਾਨੂੰ ਇਹ ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰਾਂ ___।'
quiz.explanation: ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰਾਂ is feminine plural, so both infinitive (ਪੜ੍ਹਨੀਆਂ) and modal (ਚਾਹੀਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ) must agree.

tip: Think of ਚਾਹੀਦਾ as the internal 'heart' saying should, and ਪੈਣਾ as the external 'circumstances' saying must.

title: Relative-Correlative Syntax (Jo... So / Jado... Tado)
subtitle: Joining paired clauses using Gurmukhi relative and correlative pairs
keyPoint: Punjabi forms relative constructions using bipartite pairs starting with a J-word (ਜੋ, ਜਦੋਂ, ਜਿੱਥੇ) in the dependent clause paired with a T/S-word (ਉਹ/ਸੋ, ਤਦੋਂ, ਉੱਥੇ) in the main clause.

useCases.label: Identity Identification
useCases.example: ਜਿਹੜਾ ਮਿਹਨਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਸਫ਼ਲ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

useCases.label: Temporal Synchronicity
useCases.example: ਜਦੋਂ ਘੰਟੀ ਵੱਜੀ, ਉਦੋਂ ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ਆਏ।

useCases.label: Spatial Coincidence
useCases.example: ਜਿੱਥੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹੋ, ਉੱਥੇ ਹੀ ਮੈਂ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹਾਂ।

examples.en: ਜਦੋਂ ਉਹ ਆਇਆ, ਉਦੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਸੌਂ ਰਿਹਾ ਸੀ।
ਜਿਹੜੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਮੇਜ਼ 'ਤੇ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਮੇਰੀ ਹੈ।
ਜਿਵੇਂ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਹੋਗੇ, ਉਵੇਂ ਹੀ ਅਸੀਂ ਕਰਾਂਗੇ।
ਜਿੱਥੇ ਸੱਚ ਹੈ, ਉੱਥੇ ਰੱਬ ਹੈ।

mistakes.wrong: ਜਦੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਆਇਆ, ਫਿਰ ਉਹ ਚਲਾ ਗਿਆ।
mistakes.right: ਜਦੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਆਇਆ, ਉਦੋਂ ਉਹ ਚਲਾ ਗਿਆ।
mistakes.note: Do not replace the correlative time marker ਉਦੋਂ/ਤਦੋਂ with conversational ਫਿਰ in balanced correlative sentences.

mistakes.wrong: ਕਿਤਾਬ ਜੋ ਮੈਂ ਪੜ੍ਹੀ, ਚੰਗੀ ਸੀ।
mistakes.right: ਜਿਹੜੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਮੈਂ ਪੜ੍ਹੀ, ਉਹ ਚੰਗੀ ਸੀ।
mistakes.note: Unlike English post-nominal relatives, standard Punjabi puts the J-clause first, accompanied by a matching demonstrative correlative in the second clause.

mistakes.wrong: ਜਿਹੜਾ ਆਦਮੀ ਆਏ, ਉਹ ਚੰਗੇ ਹਨ।
mistakes.right: ਜਿਹੜੇ ਆਦਮੀ ਆਏ, ਉਹ ਚੰਗੇ ਹਨ।
mistakes.note: The relative marker ਜਿਹੜਾ must inflect for gender and number (ਜਿਹੜੇ for masculine plural).

quiz.question: Wherever there is unity, there is strength: '___ ਏਕਤਾ ਹੈ, ਉੱਥੇ ਬਲ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: ਜਿੱਥੇ corresponds to spatial location matching ਉੱਥੇ.

quiz.question: When you call, I will come: 'ਜਦੋਂ ਤੂੰ ਬੁਲਾਵੇਂਗਾ, ___ ਮੈਂ ਆਵਾਂਗਾ।'
quiz.explanation: ਉਦੋਂ (or ਤਦੋਂ) is the correlative counterpart of the temporal relative ਜਦੋਂ.

quiz.question: The girl who sang well won the prize: 'ਜਿਹੜੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਨੇ ਗਾਇਆ, ___ ਇਨਾਮ ਜਿੱਤਿਆ।'
quiz.explanation: In past transitive clauses, the correlative pronoun takes the ergative case: ਉਸਨੇ.

quiz.question: As you sow, so shall you reap: 'ਜੋ ਬੀਜੋਗੇ, ___ ਵੱਢੋਗੇ।'
quiz.explanation: The traditional proverbial pair for ਜੋ is ਸੋ.

tip: Remember the J-T symmetry: relative clauses almost always start with J (ਜ-), and the main clause answers with T/O (ਤ-/ਉ-).

title: Tonal Shift & Voiced Aspirates
subtitle: Mastering the low, mid, and high tonal shifts generated by Gurmukhi voiced aspirates and Haahaa
keyPoint: Gurmukhi voiced aspirates (ਘ, ਝ, ਢ, ਧ, ਭ) and the glottal ਹ lose aspiration and convert into pitch contours: word-initial produces low-rising tone, while medial/final produces high-falling tone.

cells: Voiced stop + High-falling tone on preceding vowel
Preceding vowel shifts to open [ɛ] + High-falling tone

useCases.label: Low-Rising Tone (Initial)
useCases.example: ਘਰ ਬਹੁਤ ਵੱਡਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਹੈ।

useCases.label: High-Falling Tone (Medial/Final)
useCases.example: ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਇੱਕ ਲਾਭਦਾਇਕ ਸੁਝਾਅ ਹੈ।

useCases.label: Subjoined Haahaa Contour
useCases.example: ਉਹ ਰੋਜ਼ ਸ਼ਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ ਹੈ।

examples.en: ਧੁੱਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੈਠਣਾ ਚੰਗਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਦਰਵਾਜ਼ੇ ਦੀ ਕੁੰਡੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹੋ।

mistakes.note: Replacing ਘ with plain ਗ loses the distinctive low tone essential for semantic distinction.
When ਹ occurs medially with Mukta, standard Gurmukhi adds a Sihari (ਿ) to reflect the tonally induced open-mid vowel [ɛ].
Omitting silent medial/final ਹ removes the high-falling tonal inflection that distinguishes words like ਬਾਹਰ (outside) from ਬਾਰ (door/twelve).

quiz.question: Which word carries an initial low-rising tone replacing standard voiced aspiration?
quiz.explanation: ਭਰਾ starts with ਭ, which is pronounced as an unvoiced [p] accompanied by a low-rising tone.

quiz.question: In the word 'ਸ਼ਹਿਰ' (city), what phonetic effect does the medial 'ਹ' produce?
options: A high-falling pitch on the preceding vowel
quiz.explanation: Medial ਹ in Punjabi acts tonally, imparting a high-falling pitch contour on the preceding vowel.

quiz.question: Choose the word containing a subjoined (pairin) consonant that triggers tone:
quiz.explanation: ਚੜ੍ਹਨਾ features subjoined ਹ (ੜ੍ਹ), which creates a high pitch contour on the root syllable.

quiz.question: The final letter in 'ਲਾਭ' (profit) is pronounced with:
options: A plain [b] with high-falling pitch on [a]
quiz.explanation: Word-final voiced aspirates retain voicing but transfer aspiration into a high pitch drop on the preceding vowel.

tip: Listen for pitch rather than breath: Punjabi never breathes out heavily on voiced aspirates; it changes musical tone instead.

title: Synthetic Passive & Dative Inability
subtitle: Forming periphrastic and synthetic passives and expressing involuntary inability
keyPoint: The passive voice is formed periphrastically using the past participle followed by conjugated ਜਾਣਾ, while involuntary inability is expressed by pairing an ablative agent (ਤੋਂ) with a negative passive verb.

cells: I cannot bear to eat it

useCases.label: Physical / Psychological Inability
useCases.example: ਬਿਮਾਰੀ ਕਰਕੇ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਤੁਰਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ।

examples.en: ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਚੋਰੀ ਹੋਈਆਂ ਚੀਜ਼ਾਂ ਲੱਭੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ।
ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਹੋਰ ਝੂਠ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੁਣਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ।
ਇਹ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹਰ ਪਿੰਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।
ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਸਾਰੇ ਮਹਿਮਾਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਦਿਆ ਗਿਆ।

mistakes.note: Use the oblique possessive form ਮੇਰੇ followed by ਤੋਂ to express inability, not the direct pronoun ਮੈਂ.
The past participle in a passive clause must agree with the grammatical subject (ਚਿੱਠੀ is feminine singular, thus ਲਿਖੀ ਗਈ).

mistakes.right: ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਕੰਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ।
mistakes.note: In an inability passive, the subject must take the ablative postposition ਤੋਂ.

quiz.question: The rooms were cleaned yesterday: 'ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਕਮਰੇ ਸਾਫ਼ ___।'
quiz.explanation: ਕਮਰੇ is masculine plural, demanding agreement: ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ.

quiz.question: Because of leg pain, she cannot walk: 'ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ___ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ।'
quiz.explanation: The inability passive uses the uninflected past participle masculine singular of the intransitive verb (ਤੁਰਿਆ).

quiz.question: One should not speak ill of others: 'ਕਿਸੇ ਦੀ ਨਿੰਦਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ___।'
quiz.explanation: The synthetic passive marker inflects with ਨਿੰਦਿਆ (feminine singular), yielding ਕਰੀਦੀ.

quiz.question: Complete the impersonal passive: 'ਸਾਰੇ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ___ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।'
quiz.explanation: ਪਾਲਣਾ is feminine, requiring the passive participle compound ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਣੀ.

tip: To express 'I just can't do it' (physical or emotional incapacity), swap 'ਮੈਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ' for 'ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ' to sound instantly native.

title: Colloquial Pronominal Clitics
subtitle: Using Majhi verbal and nominal enclitic suffixes for streamlined colloquial speech
keyPoint: In colloquial and central Majhi Punjabi, unstressed personal pronouns are synthesized directly onto the end of verbs or kinship nouns as pronominal suffixes (e.g., ਸੂ, ਜੇ, ਓ).

useCases.label: Direct Ergative Contraction
useCases.example: ਰੋਟੀ ਖਾਧੀਨੇ ਕਿ ਅਜੇ ਭੁੱਖੇ ਨੇ?

examples.en: ਜਦੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ, ਤਾਂ ਕਹਿਣ ਲੱਗਾਸੂ।
ਉਸਨੇ ਖ਼ਤ ਪੜ੍ਹਿਆਸੂ ਤੇ ਰੋ ਪਿਆ।

mistakes.note: The suffix -ਸੂ already embeds the 3rd person singular agent; combining both full pronoun ਉਸਨੇ and clitic -ਸੂ in standard literary style is considered tautological.
The suffix -ਸੂ is 3rd person, while 2nd person plural honorific demands -ਜੇ.
The suffix -ਈ already incorporates the second-person genitive 'your'; it cannot be combined with ਮੇਰਾ.

quiz.question: What does the clitic verb form 'ਆਖਿਆਸੂ' mean in standard Punjabi?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ਸੂ represents the 3rd person singular agent (ਉਸਨੇ).

quiz.question: Which suffix attaches to the verb to signify a 2nd person plural/polite subject ('Did you see it?')?
quiz.explanation: -ਜੇ is the second-person polite pronominal clitic (e.g., ਡਿੱਠਾਜੇ / ਦੇਖਿਆਜੇ).

quiz.question: The form 'ਕੀਤਾਨੇ' indicates which agent?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ਨੇ corresponds to the 3rd person plural ergative agent (ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਕੀਤਾ).

quiz.question: In colloquial Majhi, 'ਚਾਚਈ' means:
quiz.explanation: The nominal clitic -ਈ attaches to kinship terms to signify 'your' (second person singular genitive).

tip: Pronominal clitics are heavily used in rural Punjab and classic Punjabi literature; spotting -ਸੂ and -ਜੇ at verb ends will help you read dialogue fluently.
